name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: Lets an AI agent open up another app, even without its source code, and explain exactly how a feature works down to the actual program instructions, so you can build something similar.
buyer: A product manager or indie developer at a small software company who sees a competitor's feature, wants to understand exactly how it works, and build an equivalent for their own product.
business_use_cases: A small SaaS team studies how a competitor's specific feature works (for example, a clever sync mechanism) and builds their own version, backed by documented evidence of how it functions.
A security researcher uses it to analyze how a native application handles data, as part of a paid, authorized vulnerability assessment engagement.
A consultant offers 'feature parity' analysis as a service: for a fee, investigate how a competitor's app does something and deliver a report plus an implementation plan for the client's own stack.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a paid competitive-feature-analysis service: investigate how a named competitor's feature works and deliver a report plus a buildable implementation plan.
Package it for security consultancies doing authorized binary and app analysis, sold as a per-seat subscription.

steal_this: This weekend, pick one specific feature from a competitor's app, use it to document exactly how that feature works, and pitch that analysis as a paid deliverable to a client building something similar. Stay on the right side of reverse-engineering and IP law here: cloning a feature too closely, rather than building an inspired equivalent, can cross into legal trouble.
